text:
A: Hello! Hi, sorry, I think I was on mute. Can you hear me now?
B: Yeah, yeah, I can hear you.
A: Oh good. I'm Nadeesha, I'm in Cardiff.
B: Hardik. Kingsbury, north-west London.
A: Nice to meet you. So, erm, I'm a senior procurement officer for an NHS health board, so contracts and tenders, that sort of thing. What do you do?
B: Supermarket. Replenishment, so stacking shelves, deliveries. Part-time, cos of school runs.
A: Oh, you have kids? I think I saw in your photo, the drawings on the fridge.
B: Yeah, my daughter. Anaya, she's six.
A: Aw, lovely. Mine is eight, Sanuli. Honestly, the school run is the worst part of my day, no? Especially in the rain. Cardiff is always raining.
B: This morning was a nightmare. Raining, bus was late, so we just walked. She was soaked.
A: Oh no, poor thing. Do you have help, or your wife, or... sorry, I don't want to assume.
B: It's fine. It's mostly me. Her mum's in Leicester. My mum helps sometimes, she's close by.
A: That's good, actually, having your mum close. My mother comes from Sri Lanka in the winter, for about three months, and it's such a relief. She takes over the kitchen completely.
B: Yeah, mine's the same. She sent me back with loads of theplas again. I've got a whole tub, I don't know what to do with them.
A: Theplas! Lucky you. Are you Gujarati?
B: Yeah. Born in Vadodara, came here at fourteen.
A: Oh, so you remember India properly. Do you go back much?
B: Not since before Covid. Flights are too much right now. I want to take Anaya to meet my grandma, though.
A: You should, sorry, I know it's expensive. We go every other year, a month in Kandy with family and then a few nights down the south coast. But the flights, honestly, I get so anxious, the connections and everything. I check everything three times.
B: Yeah, I can imagine.
A: Do you watch cricket? Sorry, that's a very Sri Lankan question.
B: Ha, yeah. India mostly. Highlights on my phone after she's in bed.
A: I can't even watch the highlights, I get too tense. My husband sends me the score and I say, don't tell me, just tell me if we won.
B: India lost the last one. I was gutted, to be honest.
A: Oh no! Well, if India are playing Sri Lanka, I'm sorry, I'll be on the other side.
B: That's fine. You lot usually lose to us anyway, innit.
A: Oh! That's very cheeky. Okay, okay, fair. Erm, what does Anaya like doing? Sanuli is all swimming, every Tuesday.
B: Lego, puzzles. And she wants a hamster. Every day, hamster, hamster.
A: Sanuli asked for a puppy. Dilan said no, I said maybe, so now I am the bad one because...
